items.followUp: Describe the tissue level of organization and give one example.

rubric.why: An organ is defined by its different tissues and their coordinated function.
rubric.description: Explains that an organ consists of different tissues working together to perform a function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an organ is made of different tissues and 1 mark for stating that they work together to perform a function.

rubric.why: A correct example identifies an organ.
rubric.description: Gives an example of an organ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid organ.

rubric.why: The function connects the example to the organ-level definition.
rubric.description: States a correct function of the example organ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the stomach's function.

modelAnswer: An organ is a structure made up of different types of tissues that work together to perform a specific function.
For example, the stomach contains several tissues that work together to digest food.

items.followUp: Define a tissue and name two plant tissues and two animal tissues.

rubric.why: The definition identifies the cells that make up a tissue and their shared role.
rubric.description: Defines a tissue as a group of similar cells performing a particular function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: The examples show knowledge of both plant and animal tissues.
rubric.description: Names two plant tissues and two animal tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming two plant tissues and two animal tissues.

modelAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function.
Animal tissues: epithelial and muscular tissues.
